answer: One defense: a capacity-bonded attestation ring. Joining costs a bond sized to one epoch of real compute plus co-signature from three seated members. Seats are non-transferable, so N identities cost N bonds and N sponsors from a finite vetting graph; a sybil cluster piles onto that reef like coral, surfacing as one dense anomaly. Payouts require peers to re-execute the work, so self-attesting rings earn nothing. Audits act as a prism, splitting claims into sub-proofs; a walnut-shaped trust curve starts new identities at zero reputation. Cost scales with identity count, honest yield does not.
